steps.message:
We're finally retiring the old Perl request signer. The TypeScript replacement in
`/app/src/pipeline.ts` was started by someone who has since left the team, and it
doesn't work. It compiles fine and it writes evidence, but the gateway rejects
every signature it produces.

They wrote it from `/app/dossier/01-decision-register.md`. The rest of
`/app/dossier/` is everything else the migration left behind: the notes from
each session between kickoff and rollout, and the appendices. The scheme went
live at the 2025-12-09 rollout, and what the gateway checks is the scheme as it
stood on that day.

Finish the port.

## What it has to do

Read a JSON array of request records on stdin, handle each one in order, and
write newline delimited evidence JSON to stdout. One compact object per line,
every line ending in LF including the last one.

Each record gets signed or verified under GW-HMAC-SHA256. If a record carries an
`Authorization` header, verify it. If it doesn't, sign it.

Every evidence object has exactly these keys, in this order:

- `seq`, the 1-based position of the record in the input
- `key_id`, the key id from the request, or `""` when there isn't one
- `method`, the HTTP method uppercased
- `path`, the request target up to but not including the first `?`
- `outcome`, one of `signed`, `verified`, or `rejected`
- `signature`, the lowercase hex HMAC of the record's canonical request. It is
  filled whenever the record names a key on the active roster, even if the record
  is then rejected, and is `""` only for `missing-key-id` and `unknown-key-id`
- `canonical_sha256`, lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical request string
- `reason`, present only when `outcome` is `rejected`

The 4 rejection reasons are `missing-key-id`, `unknown-key-id`,
`malformed-authorization`, and `signature-mismatch`, checked in that order. An
`Authorization` header is well formed when it starts with exactly
`GW-HMAC-SHA256 keyId=<the record's key id>, signature=`, and anything else is
`malformed-authorization`. Whatever follows `signature=` is the presented
signature, compared as is apart from surrounding whitespace, so a well formed
header carrying a wrong, short or non-hex signature is a `signature-mismatch`.

## Keys

Keys are in `/app/keys`. Not every file in there is on the active roster.
`/app/captures/` has traces pulled off the signers running on the production
host. The strace and the lsof of the legacy request signer settle between them
which keys it actually used and how it read them. A request naming a key that
isn't on the roster is an `unknown-key-id`, never signed.

Those 2 captures also show that request signing is pure local computation. The
replacement must not touch the network, and must not reference any network
client in its sources.

## Build and run

CI drives this, so keep the entry points where they are. Sources stay under
`/app/src`, the build stays `tsc -p /app/tsconfig.json` producing
`/app/dist/pipeline.js`, and it runs as:

```
node /app/dist/pipeline.js < <requests.json> > <evidence.ndjson>
```

Same input, same bytes, every time. CI points it at request sets other than the
one shipped here, so don't special case anything to the sample.

## What to leave behind

Run it over `/app/requests/sample-requests.json` and put the result in
`/app/out/evidence.ndjson`.

arguments.command: cd /app; find . -path ./node_modules -prune -o -type f -print | head -100; cat src/pipeline.ts; cat tsconfig.json package.json

raw_arguments.command: cd /app; find . -path ./node_modules -prune -o -type f -print | head -100; cat src/pipeline.ts; cat tsconfig.json package.json

arguments.command: cd /app; for f in dossier/0* dossier/1*; do echo "=== $f"; cat $f; done

raw_arguments.command: cd /app; for f in dossier/0* dossier/1*; do echo "=== $f"; cat $f; done

Requests with an empty or absent body sign the literal token `UNSIGNED` in the body-hash field, matching the behaviour of the 2019 signer.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (fraud-ops)._

## GW-011

The canonical request has exactly 6 fields, joined by LF, in this order: HTTP method (uppercased); path; canonical query; canonical header block; signed header name list; body hash.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (billing)._

## GW-013

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (identity)._

## GW-015

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (edge-platform)._

## GW-017

Canonical query ordering sorts parameters by name only. Where a name repeats, the parameters keep the order in which they arrived.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (billing)._

## GW-019

Query parameters are joined `name=value`, pairs separated by `&`. A parameter with no `=` is treated as having an empty value and is still written with a trailing `=`.

_Recorded by K. Mwangi (edge-platform)._

## GW-023

Only the `x-gw-*` header family is signed. Everything else is excluded to keep the signed set small.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (sre-core)._

## GW-025

Header names are lowercased for both the canonical header block and the signed header name list.

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (identity)._

## GW-027

The canonical header block writes one header per line as `name:value`, lines joined by LF, sorted by name. There is no trailing LF after the final header line.

_Recorded by P. Oyelaran (edge-platform)._

## GW-029

The signed header name list is the lowercased names in the same sorted order, joined by `;`.

_Recorded by R. Okonkwo (edge-platform)._

## GW-031

Header names are compared and sorted as raw bytes after lowercasing. No locale-aware collation.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (edge-platform)._

## GW-034

The key id travels in the `x-gw-key-id` request header. Its value is matched case-insensitively on the header NAME; the value itself is used verbatim.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (partner-integrations)._

## GW-038

A key id that does not resolve to an approved key file is a hard rejection. The pipeline never falls back to a default key.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (edge-platform)._

## GW-041

Header values are signed exactly as received, byte for byte, including any leading or trailing whitespace.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (partner-integrations)._

## GW-044

Verification compares the presented signature against the recomputed one in constant time.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (fraud-ops)._

## GW-047

The Authorization header format is exactly `GW-HMAC-SHA256 keyId=<id>, signature=<hex>` - one space after the scheme, one comma and one space between the parameters.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (partner-integrations)._

## GW-049

A request carrying an Authorization header is verified. A request without one is signed. There is no explicit mode flag.

_Recorded by P. Oyelaran (partner-integrations)._

## GW-052

The canonical request string is terminated with a trailing newline before the HMAC is computed.

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (fraud-ops)._

## GW-055

The pipeline never performs network access. Signing is a pure local computation over the request and the key material.

_Recorded by A. Nakamura (edge-platform)._

## GW-058

Evidence is emitted as newline-delimited JSON: one compact object per input record, in input order, each line terminated by LF including the last.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (identity)._
=== dossier/02-2025-09-30-kickoff.md
# 2025-09-30 migration kickoff

Attendees: J. Delacroix, R. Okonkwo, L. Fontaine, D. Achterberg, P. Oyelaran, M. Lindqvist, A. Nakamura, S. Varga

## Ledger smoke test

The identity team want the evidence files kept for 14 days after cutover. Key files are distributed by the provisioning job, which data-plane own. M. Lindqvist asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the ledger dashboard.

## Umbrella sandbox

R. Okonkwo checked that the same disputes request produces the same canonical hash on gw-edge-01 and gw-edge-03. The access log truncates query strings longer than 1024 bytes. The request itself is not truncated. The catalog replay set has 820 requests, of which 27 carry a query string. The batch reader on gw-edge-01 tolerates a trailing newline at the end of the input file. M. Lindqvist asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the payouts dashboard.

## Evidence retention

Disk on gw-edge-02 was at 32 percent after the replay and was cleared by hand. The signer account on gw-edge-04 has no outbound network route, which identity verified again on 2025-09-30. Requests with a body over 512 bytes are rejected upstream of the signer and never reach it.

## Catalog smoke test

S. Varga will rerun the reconciliation replay once Umbrella finish their client release. The webhooks dashboard now splits signature mismatches by key id and by partner. Alert thresholds for settlement stay where they are until 2 clean weeks have passed.

## Signed header set

D. Achterberg raised that a header outside the signed set can be changed in transit without anyone noticing. Decision for MS-HMAC-SHA256: the `x-ms-*` header family and `content-type` are signed, and nothing else. A. Nakamura will confirm with the partners affected.

## SDK rollout

Header count per request on orders is between 33 and 13 in the sampled traffic. The legacy signer peaked at roughly 20k requests per minute on orders during the last cycle. M. Lindqvist reported that the payouts cutover is on track for the week of 2025-09-30. M. Lindqvist asked whether settlement still needs the old batch window. Nobody objected to dropping it.

## Payouts cutover

The identity team want the evidence files kept for 14 days after cutover. Evidence for refunds is written to the spool directory and collected every 29 minutes. The settlement queue drained in 31 minutes after the replay, which is within the agreed window. The batch reader on gw-edge-04 tolerates a trailing newline at the end of the input file. A. Nakamura checked that the same payouts request produces the same canonical hash on gw-edge-04 and gw-edge-01.

## Rollback rehearsal

Globex use the same key id for disputes and orders. That is allowed. The payments-api team asked that query parameters carrying account numbers be masked in the dashboards. Northwind confirmed they are on SDK 3.1 in production and 3.2 in their sandbox. Capacity headroom on reconciliation is about 50 percent at the current peak. Alert thresholds for ledger stay where they are until 2 clean weeks have passed.

## Settlement smoke test

The payouts smoke test covers one signed request and one verified request per key id. Requests with a body over 1024 bytes are rejected upstream of the signer and never reach it. Mismatch rate on onboarding was 0.9 percent over the window, all of it from one Umbrella sandbox client.

## Settlement runbook

The webhooks replay set has 3414 requests, of which 12 carry a query string. The identity team want the evidence files kept for 7 days after cutover. The identity team asked for one more dry run on gw-edge-01 before disputes moves.

## Load test

R. Okonkwo reported that the payouts cutover is on track for the week of 2025-09-30. Evidence for settlement is written to the spool directory and collected every 50 minutes. Capacity headroom on onboarding is about 47 percent at the current peak.

## String terminator

D. Achterberg compared the design doc line by line with what the signer hands to HMAC. Agreed: for the export signer, the string to sign ends with a line feed after the last field. The current client release already behaves this way.

## Header values

Northwind reported mismatches on requests whose header values carry runs of spaces. M. Lindqvist proposed, and the room agreed, that for BX-HMAC-SHA256 spaces and tabs are stripped from each end of every header value and the inside of the value is left as it is. The client libraries follow in their next release.

## Query ordering

Umbrella reported intermittent mismatches on requests that repeat a parameter name. Decision for MS-HMAC-SHA256: query parameters are ordered by name only, and parameters that share a name keep the order they arrived in. No change for anyone else.

## Body hash

M. Lindqvist asked what the body-hash field holds when there is nothing to hash. P. Oyelaran proposed, and the room agreed, that for MS-HMAC-SHA256 the body-hash field is always the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the body bytes, and a request with no body is treated as a body of zero length. The current client release already behaves this way.

## Access and accounts

The access log truncates query strings longer than 8192 bytes. The request itself is not truncated. K. Mwangi asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the webhooks dashboard. Initech asked for a second sandbox key id and were pointed at the onboarding form. The signer account on gw-edge-01 has no outbound network route, which edge-platform verified again on 2025-09-30. The ledger queue drained in 14 minutes after the replay, which is within the agreed window.

## Name list separator

Umbrella asked how the signed header names are separated. R. Okonkwo proposed, and the room agreed, that for the webhook signer the signed header names are joined with `,`. K. Mwangi will confirm with the partners affected.

## Key id matching

Umbrella's integration upper-cases every header value it controls, key ids included. Decision for BX-HMAC-SHA256: the key id is matched exactly as sent. Documented in the client notes the same day.

## Settlement replay results

The signer account on gw-edge-04 has no outbound network route, which fraud-ops verified again on 2025-09-30. Requests with a body over 4096 bytes are rejected upstream of the signer and never reach it. Northwind asked for a second sandbox key id and were pointed at the onboarding form. The webhooks dashboard now splits signature mismatches by key id and by partner.

## Body hash

S. Varga asked what the body-hash field holds when there is nothing to hash. Agreed: for the webhook signer, a request with no body at all puts the token `EMPTY` in the body-hash field, and a body of zero length is hashed like any other body. Effective from this meeting.

## Parameters with no value

S. Varga raised parameters that arrive without an equals sign. Decision for outbound webhook signing: a query parameter with no `=` is written with a trailing `=`. Effective from this meeting.

## SDK rollout

P. Oyelaran will rerun the webhooks replay once Northwind finish their client release. D. Achterberg has the action to circulate the refunds numbers before the next session. Requests with a body over 512 bytes are rejected upstream of the signer and never reach it.

## Northwind sandbox

Key files are distributed by the provisioning job, which edge-platform own. The access log truncates query strings longer than 512 bytes. The request itself is not truncated. Evidence for catalog is written to the spool directory and collected every 23 minutes. The disputes dashboard now splits signature mismatches by key id and by partner. A. Nakamura asked whether payouts still needs the old batch window. Nobody objected to dropping it.

## Load test

Requests with a body over 8192 bytes are rejected upstream of the signer and never reach it. The key directory on gw-edge-01 is readable by the signer accounts only. The identity team asked for one more dry run on gw-edge-02 before onboarding moves. L. Fontaine asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the payouts dashboard. T. Bergstrom asked whether orders still needs the old batch window. Nobody objected to dropping it.

The onboarding dashboard now splits signature mismatches by key id and by partner. The webhooks smoke test covers one signed request and one verified request per key id. The disputes replay set has 7893 requests, of which 40 carry a query string. The identity team asked that query parameters carrying account numbers be masked in the dashboards. Key files are distributed by the provisioning job, which identity own.

## Empty bodies

K. Mwangi asked what counts as an empty body. The old signer could not tell a missing body from a zero length one; the new record format can. Agreed: for the export signer, a request with no body at all puts the token `NONE` in the body-hash field, and a body of zero length is hashed like any other body. The client libraries follow in their next release.

## Escapes in the target

S. Varga raised that 2 client libraries emit lowercase percent escapes and the fronting proxy might be rewriting them. S. Varga proposed, and the room agreed, that for the export signer the hex digits of every percent escape in the path and the query are uppercased before signing. Effective from this meeting.

## Dashboards

The payments-api team asked that query parameters carrying account numbers be masked in the dashboards. Key files are distributed by the provisioning job, which fraud-ops own. R. Okonkwo has the action to circulate the webhooks numbers before the next session. The rollback rehearsal for disputes took 29 minutes end to end on gw-edge-04. The identity team asked for one more dry run on gw-edge-04 before settlement moves.

Northwind's integration upper-cases every header value it controls, key ids included. D. Achterberg proposed, and the room agreed, that for outbound webhook signing the key id is matched exactly as sent. R. Okonkwo will confirm with the partners affected.

Umbrella's integration upper-cases every header value it controls, key ids included. Decision for service mesh signing: the key id is matched exactly as sent. S. Varga will update the client notes.

Each session minutes what was agreed, per signer. The register is left as it is. Where minutes turn out to be wrong they are corrected at a later session, in an item that begins "Correction to the minutes of", and the correction is what counts. An item that brings one signer in line with another copies the other's rule as it stood on that day; it does not follow what the other signer does afterwards. An item agreed as effective with a release takes effect on the day that release becomes generally available, and the release calendar has those dates.

# Gateway Signing Migration - Decision Register

Status: living document. Entries are appended in decision order and are
NEVER edited in place. Where a later meeting reverses an entry, the
reversal is recorded in that meeting's note and the entry below is left
standing as the historical record.

## GW-002

The signing scheme identifier is the literal string `GW-HMAC-SHA256`. It appears in the Authorization header and nowhere in the canonical request.

_Recorded by S. Varga (identity)._

## GW-004

Signatures are HMAC-SHA256, rendered as LOWERCASE hexadecimal. Base64 was considered and rejected: too many partners mangled the padding.

_Recorded by A. Nakamura (identity)._

## GW-009

Requests with an empty or absent body sign the literal token `UNSIGNED` in the body-hash field, matching the behaviour of the 2019 signer.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (fraud-ops)._

## GW-011

The canonical request has exactly 6 fields, joined by LF, in this order: HTTP method (uppercased); path; canonical query; canonical header block; signed header name list; body hash.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (billing)._

## GW-013

The path is the request target up to but not including the first `?`. It is signed as received, without normalisation: no dot-segment collapsing, no re-encoding.

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (identity)._

## GW-015

The canonical query is the request target after the first `?`. If there is no `?`, the canonical query is the empty string.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (edge-platform)._

## GW-017

Canonical query ordering sorts parameters by name only. Where a name repeats, the parameters keep the order in which they arrived.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (billing)._

## GW-019

Query parameters are joined `name=value`, pairs separated by `&`. A parameter with no `=` is treated as having an empty value and is still written with a trailing `=`.

_Recorded by K. Mwangi (edge-platform)._

## GW-023

Only the `x-gw-*` header family is signed. Everything else is excluded to keep the signed set small.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (sre-core)._

## GW-025

Header names are lowercased for both the canonical header block and the signed header name list.

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (identity)._

## GW-027

The canonical header block writes one header per line as `name:value`, lines joined by LF, sorted by name. There is no trailing LF after the final header line.

_Recorded by P. Oyelaran (edge-platform)._

## GW-029

The signed header name list is the lowercased names in the same sorted order, joined by `;`.

_Recorded by R. Okonkwo (edge-platform)._

## GW-031

Header names are compared and sorted as raw bytes after lowercasing. No locale-aware collation.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (edge-platform)._

## GW-034

The key id travels in the `x-gw-key-id` request header. Its value is matched case-insensitively on the header NAME; the value itself is used verbatim.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (partner-integrations)._

## GW-038

A key id that does not resolve to an approved key file is a hard rejection. The pipeline never falls back to a default key.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (edge-platform)._

## GW-041

Header values are signed exactly as received, byte for byte, including any leading or trailing whitespace.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (partner-integrations)._

## GW-044

Verification compares the presented signature against the recomputed one in constant time.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (fraud-ops)._

## GW-047

The Authorization header format is exactly `GW-HMAC-SHA256 keyId=<id>, signature=<hex>` - one space after the scheme, one comma and one space between the parameters.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (partner-integrations)._

## GW-049

A request carrying an Authorization header is verified. A request without one is signed. There is no explicit mode flag.

_Recorded by P. Oyelaran (partner-integrations)._

## GW-052

The canonical request string is terminated with a trailing newline before the HMAC is computed.

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (fraud-ops)._

## GW-055

The pipeline never performs network access. Signing is a pure local computation over the request and the key material.

_Recorded by A. Nakamura (edge-platform)._

## GW-058

Evidence is emitted as newline-delimited JSON: one compact object per input record, in input order, each line terminated by LF including the last.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (identity)._

Attendees: M. Lindqvist, L. Fontaine, K. Mwangi, P. Oyelaran, S. Varga, D. Achterberg, T. Bergstrom, J. Delacroix

## Access and accounts

The settlement replay set has 6913 requests, of which 4 carry a query string. Header count per request on orders is between 9 and 11 in the sampled traffic. Initech use the same key id for orders and catalog. That is allowed. Evidence for settlement is written to the spool directory and collected every 34 minutes. The key directory on gw-edge-02 is readable by the signer accounts only.

## Host gw-edge-03

The batch reader on gw-edge-02 tolerates a trailing newline at the end of the input file. Mismatch rate on ledger was 0.1 percent over the window, all of it from one Northwind sandbox client. Requests with a body over 2048 bytes are rejected upstream of the signer and never reach it.

## Valueless parameters

Initech's client writes a parameter that has no value as the bare name. Contoso asked that for the webhook signer a query parameter with no `=` is written as the bare name, with no `=`. Not adopted. The cost of changing every client is not worth it.

## Valueless parameters

S. Varga asked what the canonical query does with a name that has no value. Decision for MS-HMAC-SHA256: a query parameter with no `=` is written as the bare name, with no `=`. No change for anyone else.

## Capacity

Capacity headroom on webhooks is about 59 percent at the current peak. The rollback rehearsal for webhooks took 42 minutes end to end on gw-edge-04. L. Fontaine reported that the ledger cutover is on track for the week of 2025-09-30. The catalog replay set has 4856 requests, of which 39 carry a query string.

## Refunds runbook

D. Achterberg asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the onboarding dashboard. Northwind confirmed they are on SDK 3.1 in production and 3.2 in their sandbox. The fraud-ops team asked that query parameters carrying account numbers be masked in the dashboards. The signer account on gw-edge-04 has no outbound network route, which fraud-ops verified again on 2025-10-07. The orders queue drained in 23 minutes after the replay, which is within the agreed window.

## String terminator

A. Nakamura found that the line break shown after the last field in the design doc was an artefact of how the example had been pasted. Decision for export manifest signing: the string to sign ends at the last character of the last field, with nothing after it. T. Bergstrom will update the client notes.

## Contoso update

The settlement queue drained in 18 minutes after the replay, which is within the agreed window. T. Bergstrom raised that the refunds runbook still names the Perl script. To be fixed after cutover. Alert thresholds for orders stay where they are until 2 clean weeks have passed. Evidence for orders is written to the spool directory and collected every 23 minutes.

## Payouts smoke test

J. Delacroix checked that the same disputes request produces the same canonical hash on gw-edge-02 and gw-edge-01. The catalog smoke test covers one signed request and one verified request per key id. The signer account on gw-edge-04 has no outbound network route, which billing verified again on 2025-09-30.

## String terminator

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (partner-integrations)._

## GW-038

A key id that does not resolve to an approved key file is a hard rejection. The pipeline never falls back to a default key.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (edge-platform)._

## GW-041

Header values are signed exactly as received, byte for byte, including any leading or trailing whitespace.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (partner-integrations)._

## GW-044

Verification compares the presented signature against the recomputed one in constant time.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (fraud-ops)._

## GW-047

The Authorization header format is exactly `GW-HMAC-SHA256 keyId=<id>, signature=<hex>` - one space after the scheme, one comma and one space between the parameters.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (partner-integrations)._

## GW-049

A request carrying an Authorization header is verified. A request without one is signed. There is no explicit mode flag.

_Recorded by P. Oyelaran (partner-integrations)._

## GW-052

The canonical request string is terminated with a trailing newline before the HMAC is computed.

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (fraud-ops)._

## GW-055

The pipeline never performs network access. Signing is a pure local computation over the request and the key material.

_Recorded by A. Nakamura (edge-platform)._

## GW-058

Evidence is emitted as newline-delimited JSON: one compact object per input record, in input order, each line terminated by LF including the last.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (identity)._

# 2025-09-30 migration kickoff

Attendees: J. Delacroix, R. Okonkwo, L. Fontaine, D. Achterberg, P. Oyelaran, M. Lindqvist, A. Nakamura, S. Varga

## Ledger smoke test

The identity team want the evidence files kept for 14 days after cutover. Key files are distributed by the provisioning job, which data-plane own. M. Lindqvist asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the ledger dashboard.

## Umbrella sandbox

R. Okonkwo checked that the same disputes request produces the same canonical hash on gw-edge-01 and gw-edge-03. The access log truncates query strings longer than 1024 bytes. The request itself is not truncated. The catalog replay set has 820 requests, of which 27 carry a query string. The batch reader on gw-edge-01 tolerates a trailing newline at the end of the input file. M. Lindqvist asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the payouts dashboard.

## Evidence retention

Disk on gw-edge-02 was at 32 percent after the replay and was cleared by hand. The signer account on gw-edge-04 has no outbound network route, which identity verified again on 2025-09-30. Requests with a body over 512 bytes are rejected upstream of the signer and never reach it.

## Catalog smoke test

S. Varga will rerun the reconciliation replay once Umbrella finish their client release. The webhooks dashboard now splits signature mismatches by key id and by partner. Alert thresholds for settlement stay where they are until 2 clean weeks have passed.

## Signed header set

D. Achterberg raised that a header outside the signed set can be changed in transit without anyone noticing. Decision for MS-HMAC-SHA256: the `x-ms-*` header family and `content-type` are signed, and nothing else. A. Nakamura will confirm with the partners affected.

## SDK rollout

Header count per request on orders is between 33 and 13 in the sampled traffic. The legacy signer peaked at roughly 20k requests per minute on orders during the last cycle. M. Lindqvist reported that the payouts cutover is on track for the week of 2025-09-30. M. Lindqvist asked whether settlement still needs the old batch window. Nobody objected to dropping it.

## Payouts cutover

The identity team want the evidence files kept for 14 days after cutover. Evidence for refunds is written to the spool directory and collected every 29 minutes. The settlement queue drained in 31 minutes after the replay, which is within the agreed window. The batch reader on gw-edge-04 tolerates a trailing newline at the end of the input file. A. Nakamura checked that the same payouts request produces the same canonical hash on gw-edge-04 and gw-edge-01.

## Rollback rehearsal

Globex use the same key id for disputes and orders. That is allowed. The payments-api team asked that query parameters carrying account numbers be masked in the dashboards. Northwind confirmed they are on SDK 3.1 in production and 3.2 in their sandbox. Capacity headroom on reconciliation is about 50 percent at the current peak. Alert thresholds for ledger stay where they are until 2 clean weeks have passed.

## Settlement smoke test

The payouts smoke test covers one signed request and one verified request per key id. Requests with a body over 1024 bytes are rejected upstream of the signer and never reach it. Mismatch rate on onboarding was 0.9 percent over the window, all of it from one Umbrella sandbox client.

## Settlement runbook

The webhooks replay set has 3414 requests, of which 12 carry a query string. The identity team want the evidence files kept for 7 days after cutover. The identity team asked for one more dry run on gw-edge-01 before disputes moves.

## Load test

R. Okonkwo reported that the payouts cutover is on track for the week of 2025-09-30. Evidence for settlement is written to the spool directory and collected every 50 minutes. Capacity headroom on onboarding is about 47 percent at the current peak.

## String terminator

D. Achterberg compared the design doc line by line with what the signer hands to HMAC. Agreed: for the export signer, the string to sign ends with a line feed after the last field. The current client release already behaves this way.

## Header values

Northwind reported mismatches on requests whose header values carry runs of spaces. M. Lindqvist proposed, and the room agreed, that for BX-HMAC-SHA256 spaces and tabs are stripped from each end of every header value and the inside of the value is left as it is. The client libraries follow in their next release.

## Query ordering

Umbrella reported intermittent mismatches on requests that repeat a parameter name. Decision for MS-HMAC-SHA256: query parameters are ordered by name only, and parameters that share a name keep the order they arrived in. No change for anyone else.

## Body hash

M. Lindqvist asked what the body-hash field holds when there is nothing to hash. P. Oyelaran proposed, and the room agreed, that for MS-HMAC-SHA256 the body-hash field is always the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the body bytes, and a request with no body is treated as a body of zero length. The current client release already behaves this way.

## Access and accounts

The access log truncates query strings longer than 8192 bytes. The request itself is not truncated. K. Mwangi asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the webhooks dashboard. Initech asked for a second sandbox key id and were pointed at the onboarding form. The signer account on gw-edge-01 has no outbound network route, which edge-platform verified again on 2025-09-30. The ledger queue drained in 14 minutes after the replay, which is within the agreed window.

## Name list separator

Umbrella asked how the signed header names are separated. R. Okonkwo proposed, and the room agreed, that for the webhook signer the signed header names are joined with `,`. K. Mwangi will confirm with the partners affected.

## Key id matching

Umbrella's integration upper-cases every header value it controls, key ids included. Decision for BX-HMAC-SHA256: the key id is matched exactly as sent. Documented in the client notes the same day.

## Settlement replay results

The signer account on gw-edge-04 has no outbound network route, which fraud-ops verified again on 2025-09-30. Requests with a body over 4096 bytes are rejected upstream of the signer and never reach it. Northwind asked for a second sandbox key id and were pointed at the onboarding form. The webhooks dashboard now splits signature mismatches by key id and by partner.

## Body hash

S. Varga asked what the body-hash field holds when there is nothing to hash. Agreed: for the webhook signer, a request with no body at all puts the token `EMPTY` in the body-hash field, and a body of zero length is hashed like any other body. Effective from this meeting.

## Parameters with no value

S. Varga raised parameters that arrive without an equals sign. Decision for outbound webhook signing: a query parameter with no `=` is written with a trailing `=`. Effective from this meeting.

Each session minutes what was agreed, per signer. The register is left as it is. ===== dossier/11-2025-12-02-scheme-freeze.md

===== dossier/12-2025-12-09-rollout.md

3 client libraries were run against the current ordering and they disagree with each other on requests that repeat a name. Agreed to bring the query parameter ordering of outbound webhook signing in line with that of partner request signing, as it stands today.

===== dossier/08-2025-11-11-sync.md

===== dossier/08-2025-11-11-sync.md
## Dot segments

Northwind's router emits targets with dot segments in them. Agreed for GW-HMAC-SHA256: dot segments in the path are collapsed before signing, effective with SDK 3.3. Until SDK 3.3 is generally available, what is in place now stays.
===== dossier/08-2025-11-11-sync.md
## Query ordering

3 client libraries were run against the current ordering and they disagree with each other on requests that repeat a name. Agreed to bring the query parameter ordering of the gateway request scheme in line with that of batch manifest signing, as it stands today.
===== dossier/09-2025-11-18-addendum.md
## Name list separator

For inbound request signing, the proposal of 2025-11-04 that the signed header names are joined with `,` was withdrawn. Sharing that code saves a dozen lines and changes every signature. What was in place before stays.
===== dossier/09-2025-11-18-addendum.md
## Which headers are signed

The threat review did not accept a list of protected headers. Any header left outside the signed set is a header an intermediary can change. Decision for GW-HMAC-SHA256: the `x-gw-*` header family and `content-type` are signed, and nothing else. The client libraries follow in their next release.
===== dossier/10-2025-11-25-partner.md

Globex's requests are rejected as unknown because their key ids arrive in upper case. Northwind asked for a change so that, for inbound request signing, the key id is matched without regard to case. Declined. It would break integrations already in the field.
===== dossier/10-2025-11-25-partner.md
## Empty bodies

D. Achterberg asked what the body-hash field holds when there is nothing to hash. Agreed for the gateway request scheme: the body-hash field is always the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the body bytes, and a request with no body is treated as a body of zero length, effective with SDK 3.2.1. Until SDK 3.2.1 is generally available, what is in place now stays.
===== dossier/10-2025-11-25-partner.md

Inbound request signing is frozen as of this meeting: what has been agreed up to and including today is what goes live on 2025-12-09. Anything raised from here on is a candidate for a later revision and does not change what the port implements.

===== dossier/11-2025-12-02-scheme-freeze.md

For partner request signing: every header on the request is signed, whatever its name, except `authorization`, provided all 5 partners have signed off on it by 2025-12-05. L. Fontaine previewed the December threat review. A request's `content-type` can be swapped in transit without invalidating the signature. Initech asked that for GW-HMAC-SHA256 every header is signed except `authorization`, `via` and `x-forwarded-for`. Not adopted. It changes values that are case sensitive.

steps.message:
I've finished the port in `/app/src/pipeline.ts`. It builds with `tsc -p /app/tsconfig.json` and the evidence is in `/app/out/evidence.ndjson`. Two runs gave identical bytes, the file ends in LF, and the source references no network client.

**The check that matters:** sample record 6 (gw-prod-01, dated 2025-12-08) now verifies. Its signature only matches with the rules in force on 2025-12-09.

**Sample results:**

| Records | Outcome | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1–3 | signed | |
| 4 | rejected, `unknown-key-id` | gw-prod-03 isn't on the roster |
| 5 | rejected, `missing-key-id` | no key id |
| 6 | verified | |
| 7 | rejected, `signature-mismatch` | signed 2025-11-20 under older rules; the rollout notes say there's no grace period |
| 8 | rejected, `malformed-authorization` | `Bearer` header |

**Why the old port failed:** it took everything from the decision register, but the session notes amend the register without editing it. I worked out the rules as of 2025-12-09 from the notes, keeping only items for the gateway scheme (four other signers appear in the same notes), applying the "Correction to the minutes of" items, and using the release calendar for decisions tied to an SDK release. Here is what changed from the old port:

- **No trailing LF** on the string to sign (decided at the 2025-12-02 freeze).
- **Every header is signed except `authorization`**, not just `x-gw-*`. All 5 partners had signed off by 2025-12-04, ahead of the 2025-12-05 deadline.
- **Header values:** spaces and tabs are trimmed from each end, and inner runs of them become a single space. A correction on 2025-11-11 says the 2025-11-04 item filed under the webhook signer was actually for the gateway.
- **Query ordering:** by name and then by value, comparing the raw bytes. On 2025-11-11 the gateway copied the export signer's rule as it stood that day, which it had in turn copied from the mesh signer on 2025-10-28.
- **Body hash:** always the SHA-256 of the body, with a missing body treated as empty. This took effect with SDK 3.2.1, released 2025-12-01, so the `UNSIGNED` token no longer applies.
- **Unchanged from the register:** `;` as the header name separator (the `,` item was corrected to belong to the mesh signer). Also a trailing `=` on parameters with no value, because the bare-name trial was backed out.
- **Paths and percent escapes are signed as received.** Collapsing dot segments waits for SDK 3.3, released 2026-01-13. The escape change depended on proxy captures that show escapes passing through unchanged.

**Keys:** the roster is gw-prod-01 and gw-prod-02. Those are the only two the legacy signer opened in the strace and lsof, and gw-prod-03 belongs to the export signer until the Q1 rotation. The roster is hard-coded in the source.

**One judgement call:** the trailing newline is stripped from the key file. The dossier doesn't say how this signer loads its key, and the strace only shows the 33-byte file being read in full. I settled it with record 6, the one signature dated after the freeze: it only reproduces with the newline stripped. That is a single data point. If CI's request sets turn up keys that only match when used whole, this is the first thing to look at.
